entities.summary: Giuseppe Maria Doria Pamphili was an Italian cardinal of the Catholic Church who served as Cardinal Secretary of State from 1775 to 1797. Born into the noble Doria Pamphili family, he rose through the ranks of the Church, becoming a bishop at the age of 34 and later earning a doctorate in law. Doria Pamphili played a crucial role in shaping Catholic doctrine and policy, particularly during the Enlightenment, and was a key figure in the Vatican's diplomatic efforts. He was instrumental in negotiating the Treaty of Paris in 1783, which ended the American Revolutionary War. Doria Pamphili's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped to establish the Catholic Church's central role in European politics and society. His impact can still be seen in the modern papacy, with his emphasis on the Church's role in promoting peace and understanding. As a cardinal, Doria Pamphili was also known for his charitable work, particularly in the area of education. He supported the establishment of several schools and universities, including the Pontifical Gregorian University, which was later renamed in his honor. Doria Pamphili's death in 1816 marked the end of an era for the Catholic Church, but his legacy continues to be felt today. He was succeeded by Cardinal Fabrizio Valoni, who went on to play a significant role in shaping the Church's policies during the early 19th century.
